builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: D3D: Decoupled Diffusion Drafting for Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
summary: Replaces target-conditioned draft models (e.g., EAGLE-style or DFlash drafters) that wait for target hidden states each round with a standalone blockwise diffusion drafter that drafts successor blocks during verification, overlapped in one packed pass. Costs include training the drafter with auxiliary autoregressive supervision, extra GPU memory to hold drafter and target concurrently on one device, and added serving complexity for asynchronous scheduling and packed drafting. Can fail if acceptance length degrades outside the reported benchmarks or after pruning, negating overlap gains, and the approach depends on the open-sourced implementation matching the paper's results on your specific target model and workload.
rationale: The 5-5.7x speedup claims are strong and the code is public, but drafter training, acceptance-rate sensitivity to workload, and single-GPU memory pressure with a 32B target require small-scale validation before production adoption.
technique: Asynchronous speculative decoding via standalone diffusion drafter

claims.statement: Replaces target-conditioned draft models (e.g., EAGLE-style or DFlash drafters) that wait for target hidden states each round with a standalone blockwise diffusion drafter that drafts successor blocks during verification, overlapped in one packed pass. Costs include training the drafter with auxiliary autoregressive supervision, extra GPU memory to hold drafter and target concurrently on one device, and added serving complexity for asynchronous scheduling and packed drafting. Can fail if acceptance length degrades outside the reported benchmarks or after pruning, negating overlap gains, and the approach depends on the open-sourced implementation matching the paper's results on your specific target model and workload.
Averages 5.00x and 5.71x decoding speedup with Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B targets, up to 7.48x on GSM8K, versus 4.03x and 3.67x for DFlash, on standard speculative-decoding benchmarks.
